title: The TSPSC Paper Leak Case
dek: An insider at Telangana's public service commission and an outsourced network administrator hacked the confidential section's own computer to steal and resell exam papers — a racket that a police chargesheet says moved over Rs 1.63 crore before it was caught.

target.description: An Assistant Engineer recruitment exam, sat by around 55,000 aspirants on 5 March 2023, conducted using a question paper that remained confidential within TSPSC's own secured computer systems until the exam itself.

reality.description: TSPSC's Assistant Engineer (Civil and other disciplines) recruitment exam was held on 5 March 2023 for roughly 55,000 candidates. According to the Special Investigation Team formed by Hyderabad Police, Pulidindi Praveen Kumar — an Assistant Section Officer who also served as personal assistant to the TSPSC Secretary — conspired with Atla Raja Shekar, an outsourced network administrator in TSPSC's confidential section, to hack the password of the confidential section's computer, copy the compiled question papers onto a pen drive, and print and sell them to a network of intermediaries and candidates. TSPSC filed a complaint with Begum Bazar police on 11 March 2023, and Hyderabad Police arrested nine people, including two TSPSC staffers, on 13 March 2023; the total held rose to 49 as the SIT's investigation expanded, with one accused, reportedly in New Zealand, still at large. TSPSC formally cancelled the Assistant Engineer exam on 15 March 2023, along with the Group-I preliminary exam and two other tests, citing the FIR. The SIT's preliminary chargesheet, filed roughly three months after the leak, stated that around Rs 1.63 crore had changed hands in the sale of TSPSC papers across multiple exams. This entry has not confirmed the trial's current stage or any verdicts.
